properties.decision:
FORWARD ONLY. `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause` applies to fixes recorded from 2026-08-17 on. The 472 ChangeEvents already in the graph are NOT classified as patches or corrections, and no backfill pass will be run over them.

Anthony, 2026-08-17, answering the question directly. His own framing when he asked for the requirement was already this: "I'm not sure how many fixes have been patches ... but I'd like to start now."

WHY BACKFILLING LOSES, and it is the same reason as one rule over rather than a coincidence. Nobody remembers which of 472 changes reached its cause. A backfill would therefore be an AGENT INFERRING the answer from diffs and commit prose — producing edges that are queryable and unfounded, which dev_storyflow's finding ⑮ names as strictly worse than prose that is honestly informal. The count would look like evidence and be a reconstruction.

⭐ THE PRECEDENT IS EXACT AND WAS SET BY THE SAME PERSON THREE WEEKS EARLIER. `dec:the-authority-check-guards-forward-not-backward` grandfathered 121 of 214 settled nodes for the identical reason: the unattributed ones were bookkeeping predating the rule, not violations, and backfilling would have recorded approval 121 times on evidence no agent held. Two rules, two backfill questions, the same answer both times — which is worth noting as a pattern in how this project handles a new discipline meeting an old corpus, rather than as two unrelated calls.

WHAT THIS COSTS, stated so the trade is on the record: the useful number arrives slowly. "What still rests on a patch?" will read zero on the day the field ships and stay near zero for a while, and A LOW COUNT WILL MEAN "few fixes recorded since we started" RATHER THAN "few patches" — which is precisely the vacuous-zero this epoch exists to stamp out. So the reporting side owes a statement of its own coverage from the beginning: it must say how many fixes carry the disposition at all, not only how many were patches. That is `req:a-report-says-what-it-swept-and-whether-its-checks-ran` applied to the very first thing built under the new requirement.

REJECTED ALSO, and worth naming because it was the tempting middle: flagging past changes that LOOK like repeated patching — one artifact accepted `design_holds` many times over, say. It is computable and it is a proxy, and offering a proxy beside a real measurement invites the two to be read as one thing. If it is ever built it should be a separate, separately-labelled signal, not a way of half-answering this question.
properties.name: Recording whether a fix reached the cause binds from here, and the 472 changes already on the record are not reclassified
properties.rationale: Nobody remembers which of 472 past changes reached its cause, so a backfill would be an agent's inference wearing the clothes of a record — queryable and unfounded, the failure mode this project has already named. Same answer and same reasoning as the authority check's grandfather ruling. The cost is that the useful number accrues slowly, which is why the reporting side must state its own coverage rather than let a low count read as good news.
